title: Windows clean stop is tested: rig-service stops within 5 s on Ctrl+Break (0.6.15)
head: win-ctrl-break
body:
## What

Adds a Windows-only test that verifies `rig-service` stops cleanly and within 5 s when receiving a Ctrl+Break signal.

- New test `test_real_rig_service_subprocess_stops_within_5s_on_ctrl_break` in `tests/test_service_cli.py` starts a real `rig-service` process with `CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP`, sends `CTRL_BREAK_EVENT`, and asserts exit within 5 s with port file cleanup.
- POSIX `SIGTERM`/`SIGINT` test and new test share one helper.
- Ctrl+Break used because on Windows, Ctrl+C arrives as a console control event and `CTRL_C_EVENT` cannot target a new process group; the service already maps `SIGINT` and `SIGBREAK` to the same clean stop.
- Windows `SIGINT` skip now points at the new test; Windows `SIGTERM` skip unchanged.
- `docs/local-service.md` updated with one sentence that Ctrl+C and Ctrl+Break both stop cleanly on Windows, with CI covering Ctrl+Break.
- Version bumped 0.6.14 → 0.6.15 in `pyproject.toml`, `src/anorak/__init__.py`, `src/anorak/local_service.py`, `tests/test_local_service.py`, `tests/test_service_cli.py`, `uv.lock`; `CHANGELOG.md` Unreleased entry added.

## Checks (rerun by coordinator)

- `ruff format` clean
- `ruff check` clean
- `pytest` 600 passed, 4 skipped, 1 deselected
- `mypy --strict src` clean natively and with `--platform win32`
- `git diff --check` clean
- New test runs only on the `windows-latest` CI job

## Why the test can fail

If the `SIGBREAK` handler were missing, Windows's default Ctrl+Break action ends the process at once, so the port file stays behind and the test's port-file assert fails. This was reasoned, not run as a CI mutant.
